title: TNM Classification of Pancreatic Cancer From Unstructured Radiology Reports Using a Reasoning Language Model

live_model.evidence: "OpenAI o1 ... was used to classify the TNM classification" (Abstract); "ChatGPT's web interface was employed with settings" / "The system prompt or 'playground' tool was not used" (Methods); Table 1 confusion matrix of T-factor classification by o1 vs radiologists

prompt.location: Methods (the full classification prompt is quoted, originally written in Japanese and translated)
prompt.note: Triple quotation marks used to delimit the radiology report text within the prompt.

claim.metric: Exact-match accuracy, T-factor classification vs radiologist consensus
claim.location: Table 1 (T factor confusion matrix, o1 vs radiologists), cohort of 100 consecutive pancreatic-cancer patients

data.source: Institutional radiology reports from Tokyo Women's Medical University (IRB-approved retrospective cohort, not public)

notes: Explicitly used ChatGPT's consumer web interface rather than the API or playground; the underlying radiology reports are institutional patient data and not released, even though the prompt itself is fully printed and translated.
